classification.difficultyReason: Construct symbolic parity proofs by evaluating each composite at -x and applying the inner and outer even/odd identities in the correct order; part c requires recognising that equal inner outputs suffice without a parity condition on the outer function.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that if $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are odd functions then $g(f(x))$ is odd.

answer.worked:
Since $f$ and $g$ are odd, $f(-x)=-f(x)$ and $g(-u)=-g(u)$.
$$\begin{align*}g(f(-x))&=g(-f(x))\\g(f(-x))&=-g(f(x))\end{align*}$$Therefore $g(f(x))$ is odd.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that if $f(x)$ is an odd function and $g(x)$ is even then $g(f(x))$ is even.

answer.worked:
Since $f$ is odd and $g$ is even, $f(-x)=-f(x)$ and $g(-u)=g(u)$.
$$\begin{align*}g(f(-x))&=g(-f(x))\\g(f(-x))&=g(f(x))\end{align*}$$Therefore $g(f(x))$ is even.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show that if $f(x)$ is an even function then $g(f(x))$ is even, regardless of $g(x)$.

answer.worked:
Since $f$ is even, $f(-x)=f(x)$. Applying $g$ to these equal inputs gives
$$g(f(-x))=g(f(x)).$$Therefore the composite is even wherever it is defined; no parity condition on $g$ is needed.
